episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: AI Assistants vs AI Employees
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: An assistant helps you when you ask.
onScreen.emphasis: An employee shows up on Friday whether you asked or not.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mbella has used an AI assistant for months. It helps whenever she asks. Then she forgets to ask, and nothing happens.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An AI employee is different. It has a job, a schedule and a manager. It shows up on Friday whether anyone asked or not.

onScreen.title: AI Assistants vs AI Employees
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 6 · Hiring a Delay Analyst at Wouri Express, Douala

messages.text: Mbella: Two Fridays in a row, nobody ran the report. Everyone assumed someone else asked the AI.
Mbella: I want this to be somebody's job. Even if that somebody is software.

ui.title: Ndedi's rule
lines: It reports to me, like a junior
If it is unsure, it asks; it does not guess

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Two Fridays in a row, nobody ran the report, Tanyi. Everyone assumed someone else had asked the assistant.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mbella wants it to be somebody's job. Ndedi wants that somebody to report to her, follow her procedure, and ask when unsure.

right.title: AI employee
items: Has a role and a schedule

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An assistant waits for a prompt, answers, and forgets when the chat ends. You manage every task, every time.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An AI employee has a role, a schedule, a written procedure, memory between runs, and a named person it reports to.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: A role also means limits. What it may do, what it may never do, and who it escalates to. Write that down first.

onScreen.title: What turns an assistant into an employee

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Start with the model you already have. Give it a role: Delay Analyst. A schedule: Fridays at four. That wakes it without a prompt.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Add a procedure, Ndedi's written steps, and memory, so it knows what it found last week.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: And a manager. It reports to Ndedi, like any junior. Those five things turn an assistant into an employee.

items.text: Job: weekly delay report with causes and sources
May: read messages, read the sheet, file drafts

steps.title: The never list
steps.detail: Limits are part of the job

items.text: Name a driver as the cause of a delay
Invent a cause not in the messages

messages.text: Friday 16:00. Report drafted. One question for Ndedi: 14 messages mention “checkpoint”. New cause, or file under road?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: My role card: the job, the schedule, who I report to, what I may do. One page, in words Ndedi wrote.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: And a never list. No messaging customers, no naming drivers, no inventing causes. That is stricter than most human job descriptions.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Friday, four o'clock, I run without being asked. And when I see a new kind of delay, checkpoint, I ask Ndedi instead of guessing.

ui.title: Draft, before review
lines: Driver Moukoko: 5 of the 11, likely slow

ui.title: Draft, corrected
lines: Port queues: 11 late, Tuesday and Thursday mornings

steps.title: Why it matters
steps.detail: Employees are measured on their rules

items.text: Sources correct on a sample: yes

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Port queues, eleven late. Driver Moukoko had five of them, so he is probably slow. I recommend a warning.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: That breaks my never list. Five of eleven were on the same nine o'clock slot. The finding is the slot, not the person.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An employee is measured against its rules. Ndedi checks monthly: did it run, did it respect the never list, are the sources right.

messages.text: Week 37 report ready. New this week: checkpoint delays, filed under road as you decided. Sources attached.

ui.title: Accept week 37 report from the Delay Analyst?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Friday comes. Nobody prompts me. The report is waiting for Ndedi, with last week's decision about checkpoints already applied.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Ndedi accepts or sends it back, like any manager. The employee is accountable to her. She is accountable to Mbella.

items.label: Recruiting
items.text: Application Screener: every morning, shortlist for the manager

items.label: IT operations
items.text: Alert Reader: every hour, summarise and escalate

items.label: Accounting
items.text: Invoice Checker: every evening, flag mismatches

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Roles you can write today: an application screener every morning, an alert reader every hour, an invoice checker every evening. Each with a manager.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: The role card is written and owned by Ndedi
The company can read every run and every escalation
Drivers are never assessed by the AI employee
Accountable: the manager, then the owner

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Ndedi writes and owns the role card. Every run and every escalation can be read. Drivers are never assessed by it. Manager, then owner, are accountable.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Assistant: helps when asked. Employee: a role, a schedule, a procedure, memory, and a manager. Same model. Different job.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
